title: Learning Discrete Riemannian Metrics for Physical Fields with Cochain-Frame Equivariance
claim: Applying an orthogonal change of hidden feature basis before or after the layer gives the same result, so the layer is frame-equivariant.
layout: 2x2 commutative diagram, arrows right and down, equation callout bottom-right
description: A 2x2 commutative diagram. Each node is a small triangulated mesh with a vertex, edge and face cochain. Colored dots sit at vertices, colored stripes on edges, and colored triangles in faces. The colors stand for hidden feature channels. The top row shows the input x_k and the input after a channel permutation or rotation, x_k R^T, joined by a black arrow labeled '· R^T'. The left and right columns have red downward arrows labeled Φ that lead to the layer outputs. The bottom row shows Φ(x_k) and the same mesh with its channels reordered by R^T. The bottom-left output uses faded colors. A yellow rounded box at bottom-right holds the identity Φ(x_k R^T) = Φ(x_k) R^T. The eye goes first to the colorful meshes, then to the red Φ arrows and the highlighted equation.
caption: Metric invariance and cochain-frame equivariance. Applying an orthogonal change of hidden cochain frame R ∈O(C) before or after an RHMP layer Φ gives the same result. The frame action is on feature channels, while dk and Hk act on cell indices.
abstract: Physical fields on meshes require a separation between topology and geometry: differential identities should remain exact, while geometry, material response, and anisotropic coupling are learned from data. Existing neural surrogates often mix these roles inside unconstrained message passing. We introduce Riemannian Hodge Message Passing (RHMP), which turns this separation into an architectural principle. RHMP fixes the cellular coboundaries ($d_k$) determined by oriented incidence and learns symmetric positive-definite cochain metrics ($H_k$) for geometry-dependent propagation. The learned metric defines how cochain fields are measured and coupled; its invariance to orthogonal changes of the hidden feature basis yields cochain-frame-equivariant propagation. RHMP implements this principle with metric-weighted Hodge blocks ($d_k^\top H_{k+1}d_k$), yielding exact cochain-complex identities ($d_{k+1}d_k=0$), nonnegative Hodge energies, positive-semidefinite operators, and exact Abelian curvature invariance. Across seven physical benchmarks spanning fluids, electromagnetism, gauge fields, and variable-mesh CFD, RHMP performs strongly across these systems, with the largest gains when topology, learned geometry, and field structure interact.
